display.title: Im Yirtzeh Hashem: The Rebbe, Emunah and the Chassid Sent to Siberia (Yud Shevat)
display.summary_short: For Yud Shevat, the storyteller explains how a Rebbe strengthens our emunah, then tells how a Chassid of the Alter Rebbe learned to always say "Im Yirtzeh Hashem."
display.summary_long: For Yud Shevat, seventy years since the Rebbe became the leader of the Jewish people, the storyteller explains what a Nasi is: in every generation Hashem gives us a leader like Moshe Rabbeinu, and the main thing a Rebbe gives us is strong emunah. The hidden word "vadai" (for sure) in the pasuk "Vayevarech Dovid es Hashem" shows how a leader makes our faith certain. He encourages everyone to take on a small good resolution for Yud Shevat. Then he explains why Jews say "Im Yirtzeh Hashem" even when something seems certain, and tells a story. Yankele, a Chassid of the Alter Rebbe, borrows money from friends, with the Rebbe's blessing, to lend a poritz who wants to become an officer in Petersburg. When Yankele comes to collect, the officer has him arrested and sent to Siberia. A window closed in his face turns out to save him: the Tsarina frees everyone still waiting in line, hears his story and makes the officer pay. The Alter Rebbe explains why Yankele suffered: he promised his friends their money without saying "Im Yirtzeh Hashem."
display.lesson: A Rebbe strengthens our emunah that Hashem runs everything, so we invite Hashem into every plan by saying "Im Yirtzeh Hashem"; what seems bad may really be for our good.

date.note: Told for Yud Shevat; 'this year marks 70 years' since 10 Shevat 5710, so 5780.

advisories.note: An innocent Chassid is handcuffed, jailed and sent to a Siberian labor camp with criminals; he is freed.

characters: Potocki, the poritz who became an officer
